after.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y\sqrt{y}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+2y) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+2y) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{3/2})-\frac{1}{2}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2})+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{y}^{1/2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2y+2 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y}-y+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{1}{\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{y}-y+2}.
$$

Finally, substituting the point $(8,4),$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(8,4)} & =\frac{1}{(\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{4}-4+2)}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Given a curve $x=y+\frac{3}{{y}^{3}},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y+\frac{3}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-3}) \\  & =1+3\cdot (-3{y}^{-4}) \\  & =1-9{y}^{-4} \\  & =1-\frac{9}{{y}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{4}-9}{{y}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{4}}{{y}^{4}-9}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,1)} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{4}}{{1}^{4}-9} \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-4) \\ y & =-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{1}{2}+1 \\ y & =-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Given a curve $x=y+\frac{3}{{y}^{3}},$ what is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate $x(y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y+\frac{3}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(y)+3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{-3}) \\  & =1+3\cdot (-3{y}^{-4}) \\  & =1-9{y}^{-4} \\  & =1-\frac{9}{{y}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{4}-9}{{y}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, taking the reciprocal of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y},$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{-1}=\frac{{y}^{4}}{{y}^{4}-9}.
$$

The slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{(x,y)=(4,1)} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{4}}{{1}^{4}-9} \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the point-slope formula for a tangent line, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =-\frac{1}{8}(x-4) \\ y & =-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{1}{2}+1 \\ y & =-\frac{x}{8}+\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
